newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR EXTENDS LOSSES AGAINST HARD UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR EXTENDS LOSSES AGAINST HARD UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar extended its losses against hard currencies on Tuesday on the back of continued import pressure, dealers said.
"The dollar kept going up and down like a yo-yo today," commented one dealer.
He said the Reserve Bank intervened in the market when the local currency hit 11.1700/1800 against the U.S. dollar, nudging it up to 11.1625/1725.
But the reprieve proved short-lived with the Zimbabwe dollar closing down at 11.1725/1825 compared with Monday's 11.1500/1600.
Most dealers felt the central bank was not doing enough to support the local unit, prompting some banks to hold back money as a self-protection measure.

"The (central) Reserve Bank is coming in but not enough. We need them to come in with a big chunk and that would force those people holding onto money to off-load it into the market," one dealer said in the morning.

Against sterling the Zimbabwe dollar ended the day at 18.2760/3035 from 18.1500/1700 and eased to 6.6675/6765 versus the mark from 6.6600/6800. It was at 2.5280/5330 from 2.5100/5300 against the rand.
